components.description: For an academic appointee who becomes a parent (or has a health condition, or cares for an ill family member): a negotiated revision of duties at 100% salary for up to the equivalent of a semester, ending within 12 months of the birth or adoption; may follow childbearing leave and be extended to the end of the semester.
components.faculty_group_note: An academic appointee (tenured and tenure-track faculty, professors of practice, and senior lecturers)
components.eligible_parent_wording: becomes a parent through childbirth, adoption, or foster placement of a child (as defined by the Family Medical Leave Act (FMLA)
components.entitlement_note: R12: the duties, goals and duration are negotiated with the chair/head and approved by the dean (the Provost if no agreement); 'up to the equivalent of a semester' gives no guaranteed minimum.
components.duration_note: Up to the equivalent of a semester; when it immediately follows childbearing leave it 'may be extended to the end of a semester to accommodate teaching schedules as necessary'. Must conclude within 12 months of the birth or adoption. Also available for the member's own health condition and for care of a child, spouse/partner or parent with a serious health condition.
components.relief_note: Workload stays at 100%; the nature of the responsibilities is adjusted. The text lists, as examples, 'release from or reassignment of teaching courses, committee assignments, advising, or alteration of research duties'; which duties are relieved is negotiated, so teaching, service and advising are coded partially_relieved; research is altered, not released, and the 100% workload continues, so research is coded continues; clinical is unnamed (R4b). Not a rearrangement within the year (R16): duties are replaced for the period, not made up later.
components.time_window: must conclude within 12 months of a birth or adoption

components.description: Unpaid, job-protected FMLA leave of up to 12 weeks in a 12-month period for the birth, adoption or foster placement of a child, own serious health condition, or a spouse's, child's or parent's serious health condition.
components.eligible_parent_wording: for the birth, adoption, or foster placement of a child; for the serious health condition of the employee, the employee's parent, child or spouse
components.duration_note: Twelve weeks within a 12-month period beginning with the first day of leave (statute: 12 workweeks, 29 U.S.C. 2612(a)(1)). Military-caregiver leave (26 weeks) is not a parental purpose.
components.medical_certification_note: Certification may be required to verify a serious health condition; none is stated for leave for a birth or placement.
components.dual_employee_rule: each is entitled to twelve weeks (a married couple both employed by the state is not limited to a total of twelve weeks)
components.time_window: leave for the birth, adoption, or foster care placement of a child must begin within 12 months of the event
components.notice: Reasonable and practical notice must be provided to the agency.

sequence.note: S1: FMLA runs alongside the paid childbearing leave from the birth; the unpaid remainder (about 6 weeks) follows the paid six weeks. notes: Governing document for main-campus tenure-stream faculty: Policy 320 (faculty on less-than-12-month appointments, i.e. academic-year faculty, who receive no annual or sick leave under Policy 313). It sets the childbearing leave (c1), modified duties (c2), informal sick leave (c4) and refers to TIAA-CREF disability insurance (c5). Policy 313 and Policy 143 cover 12-month faculty and staff; their sick and annual leave components (c8-c12) are recorded with faculty_group naming that group; Policies 313 and 143 exclude academic-year faculty (c8-c11 flagged excludes_main_faculty).

Policy 352: the version in force on 2018-02-27 (amended April 2017) was not captured; 3.6 and 3.6.1 read in the 2015 capture and confirmed unchanged in the 2019 capture (version_uncertain on components citing it).

Birth parent chain: childbearing leave 6 weeks from delivery (c1, paid, with FMLA c3 12 weeks alongside from the birth) -> modified duties up to one semester, negotiated (c2, consecutive_after c1; may be extended to the end of the semester). Informal sick leave (c4) and LTD (c5) are generic plans, unlinked.
Non-birth parent chain: FMLA 12 weeks unpaid (c3); modified duties up to one semester, negotiated (c2, its link to c1 ignored for this role); tenure-clock extension one year (c6).

FMLA placement: Policy 320 s.5 says unpaid leave beyond the period of medical disability is 'available through FMLA'; coded concurrent_with the childbearing leave (S1) and flagged ambiguous on c3; if read as placing FMLA after the paid leave, birth-parent protected weeks would be 18 instead of 12.
Calendar: the documents refer to a semester (Policy 320 s.6.2) but state no length: calendar.kind = semester, and the term length follows R8's order.

Documents cited but not saved: NDSU Policy 100.1 (named in Policy 320 s.6.1 for longer-term modifications under the ADA); NDSU Policy 130 (annual leave; Policy 313); NDUS Human Resource Policy Manual Section 22 (source of Policy 135); the TIAA-CREF disability insurance plan (Policy 320 s.4); NDSU Policies 156, 168, 350.3, 350.4 and Section 353 (Policy 352; grievance, accommodation, appeals); Policies 151, 326, 332 (2019 capture of 352 only). None of these is expected to set parental leave for academic-year faculty, but Policy 100.1 and the TIAA-CREF plan could bear on disability provisions.
Policy 320 s.6.4: a period of modified duties is neither required for nor requires a tenure extension. Policy 352 4.4: an extension granted before the third-year review delays it by an equal period.
Policy 143 s.7 mentions advance sick leave up to 40 hours (discretionary) and 'shared leave'; no shared-leave programme is described in the saved documents.
